MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, February 22, 2022

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:00 PM on Tuesday, February 22, 2022, Mayor Tasha Cerda
presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney
  Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

  At 7:03 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with the
  following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council
  Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present City Manager Clint Osorio and City
  Attorney Carmen Vasquez; Police Chief Mike Saffell and Outside Counsel Attorney
  Eugene Ramirez.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION

  2.A  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL- EXISTING LITIGATION
  Gov. Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Roshawn Douglas, et. al v. City of Gardena, et al.
  United States District Court, Central District of California, Case No.2:21-cv-06327-
  JFW-MAR

  Mayor Cerda reconvened the meeting to the Regular Open Session at 7:32
  p.m., and the City Clerk noted the return of all Council Members, who were
  present at the meeting.

  When City Attorney Vasquez was asked if there was any reportable action from
  Closed Session, she stated that Item 2.A in the matter of Roshawn Douglas
  vs. City of Gardena, the City recently attended a mediation where they were
  presented with the mediator’s proposal for $60,000 subject to Council
  approval the parties tentatively agreed to that settlement on the date of the
  mediation, tonight the Council voted unanimously 5-0 to approve that
  settlement in the amount of $60,000.

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A FEBRUARY 15, 2022 MEETING
  Continuation of Environmental Assessment #14-21, Site Plan Review #5-21,
  Conditional Use Permit #5-21, and Conditional Use Permit #6-21
  The Planning Commission considered a request for site plan to construct a four-
  story residential building for 121 single room occupancy units; a conditional use
  permit to permit the construction of a single room occupancy (SRO) residential
  development in the Industrial (M-1) zone; another conditional use permit to permit
  the construction of two, six-tier automated parking structures; and a density bonus
  request to allow the density and FAR increase as the project included seven
  affordable, very low-income units. The project qualified for a categorical exemption
  from the provisions of the CEQA, pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15332 for
  an in-fill development project.
  PROJECT LOCATION: 13126 S. Western Avenue
  APPLICANT: Lee Johnson, West Realty Group, Inc

  Commission Action: The Planning Commission voted 5-0-0, approving Resolution
  No. PC 4-22, approving Site Plan Review #5-21, Conditional Use Permit #5-21, and
  Conditional Use Permit #6-21.

  City Council Action: Receive and File or Call for Council Review

  This Item was Called for Review by Council Member Francis – Mayor Cerda
  seconded it. A Public Hearing was set for the March 22, 2022, Council
  Meeting.

  10.B FEBRUARY 15, 2022 MEETING
  Ordinance No. 1840
  The Planning Commission considered an ordinance to add Chapter 18.74 to Title
  18, Zoning, of the Gardena Municipal Code relating to reasonable accommodations.

  Commission Action: The Planning Commission voted 5-0-0, approving Resolution
  No. PC 5- 22, recommending the City Council approve Ordinance No. 1840.This
  Ordinance is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  pursuant to the common sense exemption.

  4
   City Council Action: No action needed, this item will come before the City Council
  at a future meeting.

11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES – No Items

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  12.A PUBLIC HEARING: RESOLUTION NO. 6558, A Resolution amending the Gardena
  General Plan by adopting an Environmental Justice Element and an update to the
  Public Safety Plan and adopting amendments to the General Plan Implementation
  Program and direct staff to file a notice of exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines
  section 15061, Review for Exemption

  RESOLUTION NO. 6558

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE
  GARDENA GENERAL PLAN BY ADOPTING AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ELEMENT AND AN
  UPDATE TO THE PUBLIC SAFETY PLAN AND
  ADOPTING AMENDMENTS TO THE GENERAL PLAN
  IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAM AND DIRECTS STAFF
  TO FILE A NOTICE OF EXEMPTION PURSUANT TO
  CEQA GUIDELINES SECTION 15061, REVIEW FOR
  EXEMPTION

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Senior Planner Amanda Acuna and Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi
  were available for any questions.

  DeNovo Senior Planner Kelly Hickler gave the PowerPoint presentation and was available
  for any questions.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 7:48 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  There was a discussion that included our Mayor and some of our Council Members. Some
  of the items discussed were: that if the survey conducted determined that the north side
  of Gardena needs a market; there is no vacant land to accommodate the market;
  opportunities to demolition, reconstruction and refurbishment certain areas and properties;
  opportunities for developers to reimagine areas in the city; mentioned of hazardous waste
  sites and the former Brownsfields sites; in favor of the Environmental Justice Committee;
  recommendation to create an electronic dashboard to track the progress in real time;
  explanation of low rent income in order to create more affordable housing but at the same
  time not be over reliant on affordable housing; one particular census tract that is not
  labeled a disadvantaged community – how is it possible when were all in the same six
  square miles and what is unique about that tract; information provided regarding the
  Housing Element household size and disadvantaged community map; restated that what
  was once considered to be a disadvantaged community it is not solely based on income
  5
   and that the income levels have changed with the addition of the air quality element and
  living within a half mile of a hazardous site; concerns regarding the information shown on
  the Hazardous Material and Toxic Sites Map; what is the difference between chain
  markets versus independent markets. Assistant City Attorney Lisa Kranitz , Senior Planner
  Amanda Acuna, and DeNovo Senior Planner Kelly Hickler responded to all the Council’s
  questions.

  No Public Speakers

  There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 8:43 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Adopt Resolution No. 6558:

  Ayes:  Council Member Henderson and Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council
  Members Kaskanian, Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None

  13.A COVID-19 Update

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council Member Francis,

18. COUNCIL ITEMS

19. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES

  Council Member Francis

  1. Stated that the project at El Segundo and Crenshaw Blvd. has been clean but there is a
  lot of graffiti on the walls, two large trash containers and a trailer. She asked, if possible,
  when they approve a project that we request that the developer maintain the property.
  Assistant City Attorney Lisa Kranitz responded that they’ll go through the contract
  conditions and make sure that the language is included in all future projects and in the
  meantime the city will reach out to the developers.

  Mayor Cerda asked and wanted confirmation that when a developer or individual
  assumes a property, they’re the new owner and are responsible to maintain the property.
  Assistant City Attorney Lisa Kranitz confirmed that the information was correct.

  2. Asked if there’s a quicker turnaround time to disclose permitted or non-permitted
  construction work and process any permits and plans that may be required when a
  property is being sold and trying to close escrow.

  Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi explained what the city requirements
  are when a property is being sold and the permit process for unpermitted construction.

  Mayor Cerda recommended that Council Member Francis speak to City Manager Osorio
  and Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi directly so they can get a better
  understanding of the directive.

  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka

  1. Asked if we can look at what is going on with the two railroad tracks on Western and
  Normandie and possibly alleviate any issues, because he has received complaints
  regarding the railroad tracks that run from Crenshaw Lumber through Normandie, the
  tracks are lower than the street which causes issues when driving by. Seconded by
  Council Member Henderson.

20. CITY MANAGER REMARKS RE: DIRECTIVES / COUNCIL ITEMS

  City Manager Osorio gave a verbal report of information to follow-up on matters that had
  been directed or requested by the Mayor and Members of Council. Those items were, as
  follows:

  1. Memo regarding the removal of the term “alien” from city agreements. City attorney
  report on the memo that her office has reviewed all city templates on agreements and
  removed any references to the term alien.

  7
   2. Memo regarding a question on an initiative number 21-004281 which is the Taxpayer
  Protection and Government Accountability Act. The Act would amend the California
  Constitution to restrict the ability of the state counties and cities and the electorate to
  approve or collect taxes fees and other revenues.
  3. Memo regarding the explanation of the Community Development Department
  response and Plan of Action for the continued maintenance of a property located at
  12850 Crenshaw Blvd.
  4. Video presentation highlighting the Recreation and Human Services Department
  current and future events:
  • Free Shredding Event for Gardena Residents, Saturday, February 19, 2022.
  • Co-ed Youth Basketball Outdoor Skills & Drills Clinics: Freeman Park on
  Sunday February 20, 2022, and Mas Fukai Park on Saturday, March 19, 2022.
  • Free COVID-19 Vaccinations Mobile Clinic, Thursday, February 24, 2022,
  10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. at the City Hall Complex.
  • 39th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Commemorative Parade on Saturday,
  February 26, 2022. Parade begins at 10:00 a.m. at Serra High School & ends
  at Rowley Park.
  • Afternoon in the Park Celebrating Black History Month at Rowley Park, 13220
  S. Van Ness Ave., Gardena.
  • Paint in the Park, Friday, March 4, 2022, 10:00 a.m. – 11:30 a.m. at Johnson
  Park and Thursday, March 17, 2022, 10:00 a.m. – 11:30 a.m. at Rowley Park.
  • Spring Camp, April 11 – 15, 2022, Camp locations: Freeman and Johnson
  Park.
  • State of the City 2022, Thursday, March 3, 2022, at City Hall Lawn. For
  additional  information  please  call  (310)217-9507  or  visit
  citymanager@cityofgardena.org.
  • Casino Night, Friday, March 11, 2022, 4:00p.m. – 8:30 p.m. at City Hall Lawn.
  • March Madness Youth Competition, Sunday, March 20, 2022, at Mas Fukai
  Park.
  • Birthday wishes to Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi.

21. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1.  MAYOR PRO TEM TANAKA - Since the last meeting he attended the shredding event
  and lastly asked everyone to think of Officer Vela who lost his life being as being a
  helicopter observer is not an easy job. Mayor Pro Tem sent his condolences to him,
  his family, and the Huntington Beach Police Department.

  2.  COUNCIL MEMBER KASKANIAN – Had no report, only congratulated Greg T. for his
  birthday.

  3.  COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON – Thanked the Gardena Police Department for
  providing service to a family in need. Since the last meeting he attended the Count of
  LA homeless panel, District 2 meeting, Metro South Bay Vermont Corridor update
  meeting, shredding event, and the Board of Realtors event. Lastly, wished everyone
  a Happy Valentines Day.

  8
   4.  MAYOR CERDA – Since the last meeting, she attended her board meetings for the
  LA County Sanitation, and CCGA. Mayor Cerda discussed she will start talking more
  about the new initiative that will be on the ballot and would like everyone to be informed
  about the benefits to the State of California. She also shared she tried out a new
  restaurant CM chicken and commented they have the most amazing chicken.
  Encouraged everyone to try out the place. She also attended the paper shredding
  event and encouraged everyone to keep using the Gardena Direct application to report
  graffiti, furniture, and illegal dumping. Lastly, mentioned residents are leaving their
  trash cans in front of their homes and reminded everyone that trash cans are to be put
  out 24 hours before trash pickup day and to be put away within 24 hours.

  5.  COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS – Since the last meeting Council meeting, she
  attended the Los Angeles Vector Control meeting, and Homeless Count training. She
  mentioned she will be participating on the Homeless Count night. She also wanted to
  make sure everyone participates in the Dr. Martin Luther King Commemorative Parade
  on Saturday, February 26, 2022. The parade will be combined with Afternoon in the
  Park Celebrating Black History event. She also shared the grand marshals will be the
  Serra High School 2021 CIF Champions, there will also be a battle of the band’s
  competition and a drum line competition after the parade. Lastly, urged everyone that
  lives north of Rosecrans Ave. to come out and vote on April 5, 2022, at Rowley Park.

22. ANNOUNCEMENT(S)

  Mayor Cerda announced:

  1. Support Services Program for Seniors. City Staff and volunteers will assist Gardena
  seniors who are age 60+ with the following services: light housekeeping; transportation
  to appointments; grocery shopping; medication pick-up; program application and
  paperwork. For further information please contact the Senior Bureau Office at
  (310)217- 9552.

23. REMEMBRANCES

  Teresa Loan Nguyen; 92 years of age, beloved aunt of Program Coordinator Hong Lee
